claims.text: Magnetic anisotropy governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy films or nanoribbons.
Reduced dimensionality modifies magnetic exchange interactions in these FeMnNiGeSi-type nanostructures.
Dimensionality-modified magnetic exchange interactions govern magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Heat-transfer rate is limited by nanostructure geometry and the surrounding environment.
Heat-transfer-rate limitations govern magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Optimizing heat-transfer rates and nanostructure geometry will enhance the magnetocaloric response.
Optimizing heat-transfer rates and nanostructure geometry will reduce hysteresis.
The proposed behavior applies only over temperatures, magnetic-field strengths, and heat-transfer rates that preserve nanostructure stability and functionality.
